question: The 1-3-6 month rule for childhood hearing loss states: screen by 1 month, diagnose by 3 months, and fit hearing amplification or begin intervention by 6 months of age.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The 1-3-6 rule is critical: Screen by 1 month, Diagnose by 3 months, Intervene by 6 months. Missing this window means missing the critical period of auditory cortex plasticity (before age 3.5 years), which permanently compromises speech and language outcomes regardless of later intervention.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The 1-3-6 month rule is the international standard: screen by 1 month (universal newborn hearing screening), confirm diagnosis by 3 months (ABR/ASSR), and begin intervention (hearing aid fitting or cochlear implant planning) by 6 months. Adherence to this rule maximises benefit from the critical period of auditory cortex development.
